# gitmoap_repository_approval_policy (Data Source)

The approval policy and rules in force on a repository. Returns the approval switches that apply to its merge requests, the repository's own policy if it sets one, and the rules its merge requests must satisfy: every rule enforced by a group above (or the stronger version a nearer scope defines), then the nearest scope's own rules. Anyone who can see the repository may read it.

The token needs `approval_rule:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_approval_policy" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository ID

### Read-Only

- `effective` (Attributes) Who may not approve, whatever the rules say — and whether approvals survive a push. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective))
- `policy` (Attributes) A group's or repository's approval policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policy))
- `rules` (Attributes List) The rules that apply to merge requests here: every enforced rule above, as strengthened
beneath, then the nearest group's or repository's own rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `rules_here` (Attributes List) The rules this group or repository defines itself. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules_here))

<a id="nestedatt--effective"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective`

Read-Only:

- `author_can_approve` (Boolean) Whether a merge request's author may approve it.
- `committers_can_approve` (Boolean) Whether someone who authored or committed a commit in it may approve it.
- `last_pusher_can_approve` (Boolean) Whether whoever pushed its current head may approve it.
- `reset_on_push` (Boolean) Whether an approval stops counting when new commits are pushed.
